The Associated Talmud Torahs, of Phila- delphia, was established in February, 1919, with the aim of improving the educational system in the various Hebrew Schools in the city. In May, 1921, the Associated Tal- mud Torahs was reorganized, and the entire management of the Talmud Torahs was placed in the hands of a Board of Directors, functioning through the following com- mittees: Board of License. Buildings. Extension Activities. Finance. High School. Instruction. These committees, under the guidance of the Director of the Associated Talmud Torahs, are attempting to raise the level of efficiency in the Talmud Torahs, and their recommendations when ratified by the Board of Directors, are binding upon the several Talmud Torahs. The Association numbers eight elementary schools and a High School Department with nine branches, with an enrollment of 2,880 chil- dren and a teaching staff of forty - two. In all of the Talmud Torahs the greatest emphasis is laid on the Hebrew language, the study of the Bible and the Prayer Book in the original, while the study of Jewish his- tory and the principles and customs of the Jewish religion are also taught. All the schools meet five times a week, and have two or three shifts of children, each child getting between seven and ten hours ' in- struction per week. In all of them pro- vision is made for services on Friday eve- ning and Saturday morning, in which chil- dren are encouraged to participate. The Hebrew High School Department established three years ago has a Regular Department for graduates of the Talmud Torahs and congregational schools. The subjects taught are advanced Hebrew, Bible, Rashi, Mishnah, Talmud, Agadah and Religion. The Extension Department established two years ago and now con- ducted in nine centers offers instruction in Hebrew, History and Literature. The High School Department provides op- portunity to the Jewish youth of this city for an intensive Jewish education; it gives preliminary training to those who may later seek to qualify themselves for teaching in Hebrew Schools and Sunday Schools, and for leadership in Jewish clubs.
